[[File:航空神社(新橋).jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kōkū Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)|ja|航空神社 (東京都港区)|lt=Aviation Shrine in Minato, Tokyo}}]]
'''Kōkūjinja''' (航空神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shrine}} that uses “Aviation” as its name. All are famous for {{ill|Aviation safety|en|Aviation safety|qid=Q640853|lt=Aviation Safety}} and travel safety.
Since the invention of the {{ill|Airplane|en|Airplane|qid=Q197|lt=Airplane}}, the frequency of {{ill|Aviation accident|ja|航空事故|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aviation Accident|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q744913}} has increased. As a result, many—starting with military personnel—became war dead {{ill|Line of duty death|en|Line of duty death|qid=Q1036604|lt=War Dead}}, yet their spirits were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|qid=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. Therefore, to console these souls and honor their meritorious deeds at various units and schools, Aviation Shrines were established throughout the country.
== Shrines Bearing the Name "Aviation Shrine" ==
* {{ill|Kōkū Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)|ja|航空神社 (東京都港区)|lt=Aviation Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)}} – Located in {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo Metropolis}} {{ill|Minato, Tokyo|en|Minato, Tokyo|qid=Q190088|lt=Minato Ward}} and {{ill|Shinbashi|en|Shinbashi|qid=Q1347299|lt=Shinbashi}}, it is situated on the rooftop of the {{ill|Japan Aeronautic Association|ja|日本航空協会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Air Lines Association|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1770611}}’s Aviation Hall.
* {{ill|Haneda Aviation Shrine|ja|羽田航空神社}} – Located within the 1st Passenger Terminal of {{ill|Haneda Airport|en|Haneda Airport|qid=Q204853|lt=Tokyo International Airport}} (Haneda Airport) in Tokyo’s {{ill|Ōta, Tokyo|en|Ōta, Tokyo|qid=Q217234|lt=Ota Ward}}, this shrine was founded on {{ill|July 11|en|July 11|qid=Q2701|lt=July 11}}, {{ill|1963|en|1963|qid=Q2755|lt=1963}} (Showa 38) by enshrining a branch spirit {{ill|Bunrei|es|Bunrei|fr|Bunrei|id|Bunrei|ja|分霊|simple|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=Branch Spirit}} through {{ill|Bunrei|es|Bunrei|fr|Bunrei|id|Bunrei|ja|分霊|simple|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement}} from the above Aviation Shrine. Formerly, the airport branch of {{ill|Anamori Inari Shrine|ja|穴守稲荷神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anamori Inari Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11597221}} was also relocated nearby; however, during the terminal relocation in {{ill|1993|en|1993|qid=Q2065|lt=1993}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}5), it was merged into the main shrine.
* Aviation Shrine – Located in Akebonochō, {{ill|Tachikawa, Tokyo|en|Tachikawa, Tokyo|qid=Q269634|lt=Tachikawa City}}, Tokyo. It is said to have originated when a local influential person enshrined {{ill|Kitano Tenmangu|ja|京都北野天満宮}} as a ward against unlucky directions, and later, at the request of the Army Air Force’s 5th Squadron, consolidated the aviation war dead.
* Aviation Shrine – Situated in Kawajiri, Midori Ward ({{ill|Sagamihara|en|Sagamihara|qid=Q209779|lt=Sagamihara City}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|qid=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}}), this shrine was established to console the souls of fallen crew: on March 23, {{ill|1941|en|1941|qid=Q5231|lt=1941}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Showa}}16) a twin-engine reconnaissance aircraft crashed and burst into flames killing two crew members, and on April 8, {{ill|1944|en|1944|qid=Q5268|lt=1944}} (Showa 19) a Japanese Army Hayabusa fighter crashed with its pilot perishing.
* {{ill|Sanctuaire de l'aviation (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aviation Shrine (Tokorozawa)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q124483190}} – Located at the {{ill|Kitano Tenjinsha|ja|北野天神社 (所沢市)|lt_dep=北野天神社|lt_ja=北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenmangu (Tokorozawa)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11404276}} in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}} {{ill|Tokorozawa, Saitama|en|Tokorozawa, Saitama|qid=Q165857|lt=Tokorozawa}}, in the area of {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Motomachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11460790}}. It was founded on September 25, Showa 12 by fulfilling the wish of {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|qid=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi}}, who, having received sacred wood from the construction of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingu}} and materials from {{ill|Hikawa Shrine (Saitama)|abstract|Q703633|az|Hikava məbədi (Saytama)|de|Hikawa-Schrein|es|Santuario Hikawa|eu|Hikawa Jinja|fr|Hikawa-jinja|hu|Hikava szentély (Szaitama)|it|Santuario di Hikawa|ja|氷川神社|ko|히카와 신사|la|Templum Hikawa|sh|Hikawa hram (Saitama)|tr|Hikawa Tapınağı|zh|冰川神社|qid=Q703633|lt=Hikawa Shrine}}, built a shrine at the southern end of the {{ill|Tokorozawa Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokorozawa Army Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11658682}} to enshrine {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} and to conduct ceremonies for the aviation war dead. At that time, because aviation war dead were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|qid=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}, they were venerated as protective deities of the nation. In Showa 13, the shrine was transferred to the premises of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|en|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|qid=Q2822344|lt=Army Aviation Officer School}} established in Toyooka (now part of the Japan Air Self-Defense Force’s {{ill|Iruma Air Base|en|Iruma Air Base|qid=Q3015843|lt=Iruma Base}}), becoming the center of reverence for its students. When the school grounds were seized by the U.S. military at the end of the war in Showa 20, aviation officials led by the school’s head {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|qid=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi}} petitioned to preserve the shrine permanently. With the cooperation of local volunteers and the chief priest, Ryōsuke Kurihara, of the long-serving {{ill|Kitano Tenjinsha|ja|北野天神社 (所沢市)|lt_dep=北野天神社|lt_ja=北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenmangu (Tokorozawa)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11404276}}, the enshrinement was transferred in its original form on September 3, Showa 20, to the current {{ill|Kitano Tenjinsha|ja|北野天神社 (所沢市)|lt_dep=北野天神社|lt_ja=北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenmangu (Tokorozawa)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11404276}}. Ceremonies have continued unceasingly ever since, with visits from local citizens, Prince Higashikuni, the governor of Saitama Prefecture, the mayor of Tokorozawa, successive heads of the Army Aviation Officer School, and Japan’s first official domestic flight pioneer, Tokugawa Yoshitoshi. After the establishment of the Air Self-Defense Force in 1954 (Showa 29), war dead personnel were enshrined at this Aviation Shrine (with branch enshrinements following the construction of the Defense Agency Memorial Monument). On November 19, {{ill|1965|en|1965|qid=Q2650|lt=1965}} (Showa 40), the spirit tablet was transferred to the Air Self-Defense Force Candidate School, then on February 26, {{ill|1988|en|1988|qid=Q2426|lt=1988}} (Showa 63) to the Air Self-Defense Force Iruma Base Shūbudai Memorial Hall. On March 13, {{ill|2024|en|2024|qid=Q49619|lt=2024}} (Reiwa 6), the spirit tablet was again transferred and enshrined at Kitano Tenmangu, and from April 13, {{ill|2024|en|2024|qid=Q49619|lt=2024}} (Reiwa 6) onward, the issuance of goshuin and aviation safety charms began.

wikidata|qid=Q47392910}}, this shrine was originally established in {{ill|1937|en|1937|qid=Q18647|lt=1937}} (Showa 12) by aviation pioneer {{ill|Otojirô Itô|en|Otojirô Itô|qid=Q11380502|lt=Itō Otojirō}} to enshrine the war dead of the early aviation era—including his eldest son Shintarō and the celebrated aviator {{ill|Yamagata Toyotaro|ja|山縣豊太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamagata Toyotaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q110774379}}—at the factory premises ({{ill|Factory|en|Factory|qid=Q83405|lt=Factory}} and {{ill|site|ja|敷地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Premises|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11499678}}) of {{ill|Itō Aircraft Manufacturing|ja|伊藤飛行機研究所|lt_dep=Itō Aircraft Factory|lt_ja=伊藤飛行機製作所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itō Aircraft Manufacturing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11380505}} in Tsudanuma, {{ill|Chiba District, Chiba|en|Chiba District, Chiba|qid=Q5095301|lt=Chiba District}}’s Tsudanuma Town (now part of {{ill|Narashino|en|Narashino|qid=Q318047|lt=Narashino}}) in Saginuma. Following Japan’s defeat ({{ill|Surrender of Japan|en|Surrender of Japan|qid=Q6540361|lt=Japan's War Defeat}}), Itō, forced out of the aviation industry, became a farmer in the eastern peak area of Toyama Village (now part of Narita City) in {{ill|Tōyama|ja|遠山村 (千葉県)|lt_dep=遠山村|lt_ja=遠山村|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyama Village|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11642044}} through postwar development ({{ill|Postwar Development|ja|戦後開拓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Postwar Development|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11496073}}). After some time, the local community decided to build a shrine, and on November 23, {{ill|1953|en|1953|qid=Q18585|lt=1953}} (Showa 28) the shrine was relocated. At that time, a new enshrinement of {{ill|Ninomiya Sontoku|en|Ninomiya Sontoku|qid=Q968964|lt=Ninomiya Sontoku}} was made from {{ill|Hōtoku Ninomiya Shrine|en|Hōtoku Ninomiya Shrine|qid=Q11428033|lt=Hōtoku Ninomiya Shrine}} of {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|qid=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}}. Later, the shrine was renamed “Tōhō Shrine” and came to be revered by the local settlers as the guardian shrine ({{ill|Ujigami|en|Ujigami|qid=Q767655|lt=Ujigami}}) of their new community. However, with the construction of the new Tokyo International Airport (now {{ill|Narita International Airport|en|Narita International Airport|qid=Q36454|lt=Narita International Airport}}), in September 2001 (Heisei 13) at the request of Itō Otojirō’s family, the spirit of Ninomiya Sontoku was retained and transferred to the outdoor display area of the Aviation Science Museum in Shibayama Town, Sanbu District, Chiba Prefecture. The shrine’s {{ill|Omamori|en|Omamori|qid=Q1756788|lt=Amulet}} is available at the museum’s shop.
* {{ill|Japan Aviation High School|en|Japan Aviation High School|qid=Q576350|lt=Japan Air High School}} – Located in Utsutani, {{ill|Kai, Yamanashi|en|Kai, Yamanashi|qid=Q577309|lt=Kai City}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|qid=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture}}, this shrine is enshrined within the campus of Japan Air High School.
* {{ill|Japan Aviation High School Ishikawa|ja|日本航空高等学校石川|lt_dep=Aviation Shrine (Noto)|lt_ja=能登航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Air High School Ishikawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11509002}} – Located in Suuei, Mitsuimachi, {{ill|Wajima, Ishikawa|en|Wajima, Ishikawa|qid=Q823896|lt=Wajima City}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|en|Ishikawa Prefecture|qid=Q131281|lt=Ishikawa Prefecture}}, this shrine is enshrined within the campus of Japan Air High School Ishikawa.
* {{ill|Senshu Aviation Shrine|ja|泉州航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senshu Aviation Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17995313}} – Located in Kamikawaya, {{ill|Izumisano|en|Izumisano|qid=Q852018|lt=Izumisano}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, this shrine was established by branching off from the {{ill|Iwafune Shrine|ja|磐船神社 (交野市)|lt_dep=磐船神社|lt_ja=磐船神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwafune Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11587926}} of the private municipality in {{ill|Katano|en|Katano|qid=Q819646|lt=Katano City}}, on the occasion of constructing {{ill|Kansai International Airport|en|Kansai International Airport|qid=Q193682|lt=Kansai International Airport}}. It is dedicated to prayers for aviation safety and travel safety; its official name is “Senshu Iwafune Shrine.”
* {{ill|Takayama Kouku Park|ja|高山航空公園|lt_dep=Takayama Aviation Shrine|lt_ja=高山航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takayama Aviation Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11669430}} – Located in Higashibun Otsu, {{ill|Ayauta District, Kagawa|en|Ayauta District, Kagawa|qid=Q1123066|lt=Ayauta District}}, {{ill|Ayagawa, Kagawa|en|Ayagawa, Kagawa|qid=Q1156043|lt=Ayagawa Town}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|en|Kagawa Prefecture|qid=Q161454|lt=Kagawa Prefecture}}, this shrine was founded on December 16, {{ill|1990|en|1990|qid=Q2064|lt=1990}} (Heisei 2) in conjunction with the development of Takayama Aviation Park, prompted by airplanes flying over after the completion of {{ill|Takamatsu Airport|en|Takamatsu Airport|qid=Q1334603|lt=Takamatsu Airport}}, as a prayer for the safety of air transportation. Next to the shrine stand an Army Youth Aviator Memorial Monument, established by volunteers from Kagawa Prefecture, and an ancient local earth god’s shrine. Since its enshrinement, successive {{ill|Minister of Transport of Japan|ja|運輸大臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minister of Transport|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11640486}}s and {{ill|Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism|en|Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism|qid=Q842012|lt=Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism}} have visited, with commemorative tree plantings around it.
== Shrines Closely Associated with Aviation ==
* {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)|ja|金刀比羅宮 (東京都港区)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Minato, Tokyo)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11646485}} – Located in {{ill|Toranomon|en|Toranomon|qid=Q7825412|lt=Toranomon}}, Minato Ward, Tokyo, it was established when {{ill|Kyōgoku Takakazu|ja|京極高和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyogoku Takakazu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11374457}}—the feudal lord of {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province}} and the {{ill|Marugame Domain|en|Marugame Domain|qid=Q10863480|lt=Marugame Domain}}—enshrined {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|qid=Q94760|lt=Kotohira Daigongen}} at his Edo residence.
* {{ill|Anamori Inari Shrine|ja|穴守稲荷神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anamori Inari Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11597221}} – Located in {{ill|Haneda, Ōta, Tokyo|en|Haneda, Ōta, Tokyo|qid=Q1494212|lt=Haneda}}, Ota Ward, Tokyo. The area now occupied by {{ill|Haneda Airport|en|Haneda Airport|qid=Q204853|lt=Tokyo International Airport}} (specifically, {{ill|Haneda Airport|ja|羽田空港 (大田区)|lt_dep=羽田空港|lt_ja=羽田空港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haneda Airport|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11610321}}) was once part of the grounds and monzen town of this shrine until {{ill|1945|en|1945|qid=Q5240|lt=1945}} (Showa 20). Even before the opening of {{ill|Tokyo Airfield|ja|東京飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q128845377}} in {{ill|1931|en|1931|qid=Q18782|lt=1931}} (Showa 6), during the {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taisho Era}}, there is an account of flight school trainees in the monzen praying for safety. It remains the shrine nearest to the airport and was originally founded to protect Haneda Airport ({{ill|Suzuki Shinden|ja|鈴木新田 (大田区)}}) from disaster. As an airport-protecting shrine, it attracts prayers for safety from the aviation industry, related government agencies, and travelers. Additionally, on the roof of the old Haneda Airport Terminal Building (prior to offshore expansion), both Haneda Aviation Shrine and the Anamori Inari Shrine Airport Branch were enshrined; even now, branch spirits are maintained on the grounds of the {{ill|Japan Airlines|en|Japan Airlines|qid=Q213140|lt=Japan Air Lines}} Main Maintenance Center and the {{ill|San-Ai Oil|en|San-Ai Oil|qid=Q7413196|lt=Sanei Oburi}} Haneda branch. {{Main|穴守稲荷神社#羽田空港（航空業界）との関係|qq=}}
* {{ill|Ikazuchi Shrine(Yokosuka)|ja|雷神社 (横須賀市)|lt_dep=浜空神社|lt_ja=浜空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hamakū Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11660191}} – Located in {{ill|Yokosuka|en|Yokosuka|qid=Q200578|lt=Yokosuka City}}’s {{ill|Oppama-honchō|ja|追浜本町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oihama Honmachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q122148344}}, Kanagawa Prefecture. After being seized by the U.S. military post-war and released in {{ill|1971|en|1971|qid=Q2475|lt=1971}} (Showa 46), the comrades association “Hamakū-kai” restored the damaged Torifune Shrine and, as “Hamakū Shrine,” held memorial services for fallen members. Eventually, due to aging, the association relocated the shrine building to {{ill|Yokosuka Raijin Shrine|ja|横須賀雷神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokosuka Raijin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135503394}} in {{ill|2008|en|2008|qid=Q2004|lt=2008}} (Heisei 20) and erected a memorial monument inscribed with “Rest in Peace, Navy Seaplane Corps” on the former site.
* {{ill|Fukami Shrine|ja|深見神社|lt_dep=靖國社|lt_ja=靖國社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yasukuni Shrine (as associated with Yasukuni)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11560278}} – Located in Fukami, {{ill|Yamato, Kanagawa|en|Yamato, Kanagawa|qid=Q386697|lt=Yamato City}}, Kanagawa Prefecture, this shrine is the subsidiary of {{ill|Fukami Shrine|ja|深見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukami Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11560278}}. It was once enshrined within the {{ill|Atsugi Navy Air Corps Base|ja|厚木海軍航空隊|lt_dep=厚木海軍航空隊基地|lt_ja=厚木海軍航空隊基地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atsugi Navy Air Corps Base|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11409262}} (currently {{ill|Naval Air Facility Atsugi|ja|厚木基地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atsugi Base|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 厚木海軍飛行場|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3016710}}) and was known as Atsugi Air Shrine, enshrining the war dead register of the Atsugi Navy Air Corps along with a treasured sword bestowed by Yasukuni Shrine.
* {{ill|Tōhō Shrine|ja|東峰神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhō Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11526776}} – Located in {{ill|Narita, Chiba|en|Narita, Chiba|qid=Q273798|lt=Narita City}}’s {{ill|Tōhō|ja|東峰 (成田市)|lt_dep=東峰|lt_ja=東峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q47392901}}, Chiba Prefecture, it is set within the grounds of the Aviation Science Museum, where Ninomiya Sontoku was enshrined alongside the spirit of the Aviation Shrine. In {{ill|2001|en|2001|qid=Q1988|lt=2001}} (Heisei 13), the spirit of the Aviation Shrine was transferred to the museum’s outdoor display area in {{ill|Iwayama|ja|岩山 (芝山町)|lt_dep=岩山|lt_ja=岩山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q47392910}}, Shibayama Town, Sanbu District, Chiba Prefecture.

* {{ill|Shimomasuda Shrine|abstract|Q11360748|ja|下増田神社|qid=Q11360748}} – Situated at the Shimomasuda Mansion in {{ill|Natori, Miyagi|en|Natori, Miyagi|qid=Q642018|lt=Natori City}}, Miyagi Prefecture, it enshrines an aviation shrine originally established in {{ill|1939|en|1939|qid=Q18639|lt=1939}} (Showa 14) at the former {{ill|Sendai Army Flying School|ja|仙台陸軍飛行学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Army Flying School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11378081}}.

It was founded on November 13, {{ill|1944|en|1944|qid=Q5268|lt=1944}} (Showa 19) within the Second Education Unit of the {{ill|Gifu Army Aviation Maintenance School|ja|岐阜陸軍航空整備学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gifu Army Aviation Maintenance School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11471899}}, enshrined as the guardian for students of aviation technology, later transferred to the grounds of Mizonokiba Shrine, and eventually merged with the spirits of the school’s graduates (boy pilots).
* {{ill|Asahi Inari Shrine|ja|朝日稲荷神社 (各務原市)|lt_dep=朝日稲荷神社|lt_ja=朝日稲荷神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asahi Inari Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q112336630}} – Located in {{ill|Kakamigahara|ar|كاكاميغهارا (غيفو)|arz|كاكاميجاهارا, جيفو|azb|کاکامیقاهارا، قیفو|ca|Kakamigahara|ce|Какамигахара|ceb|Kakamigahara (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Kakamigahara|de|Kakamigahara|eo|Kakamigahara|es|Kakamigahara (Gifu)|fa|کاکامیگاهارا، گیفو|fi|Kakamigahara|fr|Kakamigahara|gl|Kakamigahara|it|Kakamigahara|ja|各務原市|ko|가카미가하라시|mg|Kakamigahara|mr|काकामिगहारा|mzn|کاکامیگاهارا، گیفو|nl|Kakamigahara|no|Kakamigahara|pl|Kakamigahara|pt|Kakamigahara|ro|Kakamigahara|ru|Какамигахара|sh|Kakamigahara|sr|Какамигахара|su|Kakamigahara, Gifu|sv|Kakamigahara|tg|Какамигаҳара|tl|Kakamigahara, Gifu|tr|Kakamigahara|tt|Какамигахара|uk|Какаміґахара|ur|کاکامیگاہارا، گیفو|vi|Kakamigahara, Gifu|war|Kakamigahara, Gifu|zh|各务原市|zh_classical|各務原市|zh_min_nan|Kakamigahara-chhī|zh_yue|各務原|qid=Q641491|lt=Kakamigahara City}}’s {{ill|Unuma Asahimachi|ja|鵜沼朝日町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Unuma Asahimachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q131870043}}, Gifu Prefecture, this shrine was established as an aviation shrine at the Imperial Japanese Army’s base (displayed as {{ill|Gifu Air Field|en|Gifu Air Field|qid=Q3275507|lt=Gifu Base}}) and was later renamed when relocated after the war.
* {{ill|Kuga Shrine|ja|久我神社 (京都市北区)|lt_dep=久我神社|lt_ja=久我神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuga Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11369376}} – Located in Shichikitanakedera-chō, {{ill|Kita-ku, Kyoto|en|Kita-ku, Kyoto|qid=Q1154970|lt=Kita Ward}}, Kyoto City, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|qid=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}, this shrine is an affiliate of {{ill|Kamigamo Shrine|en|Kamigamo Shrine|qid=Q700448|lt=Kamobetsu Raijin Shrine}} and enshrines Kamo Tatemune of the {{ill|Kamo clan|en|Kamo clan|qid=Q2975287|lt=Kamo Clan}} (associated with {{ill|Yatagarasu|en|Yatagarasu|qid=Q745463|lt=Yatagarasu}}). It is especially venerated for conferring benefits in “traffic safety” and “aviation safety.”
* {{ill|Hikō Shrine|ja|飛行神社}} – Located in Hachiman Doi, {{ill|Yawata|en|Yawata|qid=Q260923|lt=Yawata City}}, Kyoto Prefecture, it was founded in {{ill|1915|en|1915|qid=Q2084|lt=1915}} (Taisho 4) by {{ill|Chūhachi Ninomiya|en|Chūhachi Ninomiya|qid=Q3655885|lt=Ninomiya Tada-hachi}}, the first in Japan to study the principles of flight. Pained by the frequent aviation accidents since the invention of the airplane, he felt responsible for memorializing the victims of such tragedies and invested his personal funds to enshrine their spirits. It now attracts many visitors from the aviation and aerospace sectors seeking safety prayers.
* {{ill|Iwafune Shrine|ja|磐船神社 (交野市)|lt_dep=磐船神社|lt_ja=磐船神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwafune Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11587926}} – Located in the private municipality of {{ill|Katano|en|Katano|qid=Q819646|lt=Katano City}}, Osaka Prefecture, this shrine enshrines the god of airplanes, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}}, and also houses the enshrined spirits of aviation disaster victims ({{ill|Enshrinement Together|ja|合祀}}).
* {{ill|Yata ni Imasu Kushitamahiko Shrine|ja|矢田坐久志玉比古神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yatadazaku Shitamahiko Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11584205}} – Situated in Yata Town, {{ill|Yamatokōriyama|en|Yamatokōriyama|qid=Q118213|lt=Yamato-Koriyama}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}, the deity enshrined here, Kushidama Nigihayahi, is revered as the progenitor of aviation based on the legend recorded in the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}, which tells of him riding on a heavenly Iwafune and flying through the sky. An aviation festival is held every September 20, and a dedicated propeller hangs from the loft of the gatehouse.
* Kamikaze Shrine – Located in {{ill|Nishinomiya|en|Nishinomiya|qid=Q243853|lt=Nishinomiya City}}’s {{ill|Uegahara|ja|上ケ原山田町|lt_dep=上ケ原|lt_ja=上ケ原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigahara Yamada Town|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上ケ原|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q122451456}}, Hyōgo Prefecture, it once served as the in-house shrine of the {{ill|Nishinomiya Navy Air Corps|ja|西ノ宮海軍航空隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishinomiya Navy Air Corps|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11627661}}. Before the post-war incineration, local residents risked their lives to relocate it into {{ill|Kamigahara Hachiman Shrine|ja|上ケ原八幡神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigahara Hachiman Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135503396}}.
* {{ill|Kotohira-gū|en|Kotohira-gū|qid=Q94760|lt=Kotohira Shrine}} – Located in Kawanishi, Kotohira Town, {{ill|Nakatado District, Kagawa|en|Nakatado District, Kagawa|qid=Q1206155|lt=Nakatado District}}, Kagawa Prefecture, it is revered as the god of safe navigation and maritime protection, with its veneration later extending to land, sea, and aviation traffic safety.
* Ninomiya Flying Shrine – Situated in {{ill|Mannō, Kagawa|en|Mannō, Kagawa|qid=Q1350204|lt=Mannou Town}}, Nakatado District, Kagawa Prefecture, at Oitsugi near {{ill|Mominoki Pass|ja|樅ノ木峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononoki Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24876464}}, it was founded in {{ill|1991|en|1991|qid=Q2062|lt=1991}} (Heisei 3) at the site where Tada-hachi is said to have first conceived the principles of flight.
